title: The specified finite direct-image compositor preserves the ordinary counit and its projection mate
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum $A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-pur-conventions]. Let $U\xrightarrow{h}V\xrightarrow{g}W$ be proper morphisms between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories of constant-$A$ modules on the small pro-etale sites, and the actual pullbacks, direct images and adjunctions $P_t=Lt^*\dashv R_t=Rt_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], for $t=h,g,gh$. Let $a:P_{gh}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_hP_g$ be the canonical pullback compositor [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], and let
$$c=c_{g,h}:R_{gh}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_gR_h$$
be exactly the finite direct-image compositor of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition], obtained by deriving the underived fibre-product-pasting map, not an unspecified isomorphism. Then $c^{-1}$ is conjugate to $a$ under these derived adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. In particular, writing $\varepsilon_t:P_tR_t\to1$ for the specified ordinary counits, for every $M\in D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ the equality of actual maps $P_{gh}R_{gh}M\to M$ is
$$\varepsilon_{gh,M}=\varepsilon_{h,M}\circ P_h(\varepsilon_{g,R_hM})\circ a_{R_gR_hM}\circ P_{gh}(c_M).$$
Let $\pi_t$ be the counit-defined projection map of [def-exchange-projection] and let $d_{M,N}:M\otimes_A^LP_{gh}N\xrightarrow{\sim}M\otimes_A^LP_hP_gN$ be $1_M\otimes a_N$, using the tensor-pullback comparisons of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. For arbitrary $M\in D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $N\in D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, the resulting compositor-normalized projection identity is
$$R_gR_h(d_{M,N})\circ c_{M\otimes_A^LP_{gh}N}\circ\pi_{gh;M,N}
=R_g(\pi_{h;M,P_gN})\circ\pi_{g;R_hM,N}\circ(c_M\otimes1_N).$$
These identities are natural in their derived arguments. Under the canonical identity identifications they also hold if either proper map is an identity; the corresponding identity projection is the identity. They do not require boundedness, etale origin, constructibility, or finite Tor amplitude and invert no projection map.

proof.text: Write $p_t=t^*$ and $r_t=t_*$ for the ordinary module functors of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Their coefficient maps are the canonical constant-$A$ identifications, so all $p_t$ are exact. Let $b:r_{gh}\cong r_gr_h$ be the specified ordinary fibre-product-pasting comparison. On sections over $T\to W$, it is induced by $U\times_WT\cong U\times_V(V\times_WT)$; both structural maps to the constant coefficient ring agree. Under the composite ordinary adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], the conjugate of $b^{-1}$ is the ordinary pullback comparison $a^0:p_{gh}\cong p_hp_g$. Indeed the two successive adjunction bijections insert the two pullback units, and, after the displayed fibre-product identification, the single unit has that same value. In the tensor presentation of module pullback this sends $m\otimes r$ to $(m\otimes1)\otimes r$, with inverse $(m\otimes s)\otimes r\mapsto m\otimes c_h(s)r$; balancing verifies both inverses and the equality of units. This is precisely the termwise comparison specified in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], not an arbitrary isomorphism between the pullbacks.

source.place: Tags 03D8 (sites-modules.tex, lemma-push-pull-composition-modules) and 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition); ordinary module adjunction and its units

proof.text: Choose a K-injective representative $I$ of $M$ by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], on the small site model specified by the operations. Since $p_h,p_g,p_{gh}$ are exact left adjoints, [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] makes $r_hI$, $r_gr_hI$ and $r_{gh}I$ K-injective. Thus the specified $R_hM,R_gR_hM,R_{gh}M$ are represented by these complexes. In the normalization of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] take $j:r_hI\to J$ to be the identity, since $r_hI$ is already K-injective. Here $(gh)_*I$ and $g_*h_*I$ are identified by $b_I$, so the class of $g_*j=\mathrm{id}$ in that normalization is $Q(b_I)$. The item specifies $c$ as the comparison of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] obtained by deriving the underived fibre-product-pasting map $b$; with the K-injective representatives just chosen this derived map is $Q(b_I):Q((gh)_*I)\to Q(g_*h_*I)$. Hence $c_M=Q(b_I)$ after the canonical resolution identifications. Only this stated specification of $c$ is used, not the construction inside the cited lemma's proof. There is no assertion that ordinary direct image is exact: only its preservation of K-injectives is used.

For any derived input on $W$, choose a K-flat representative $K$ with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Then [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] gives the ordinary adjunction bijections $a_h$ on homotopy classes. The derived bijection of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] is the canonical bijection $e$ of [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general], characterized by $e(p_s\circ Q(f)\circ Q(t)^{-1})=Q(s)^{-1}\circ Q(a_h(f))\circ u_t$; take $s=\mathrm{id}$ on the K-injective target and $t=\mathrm{id}$ on $K$, which is allowed since the pullbacks are exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], localization identifies maps into each of $I,r_hI,r_gr_hI,r_{gh}I$ with those homotopy classes. Hence the actual derived adjunction bijection for $P_{gh}\dashv R_{gh}$ is computed by the ordinary bijection on $p_{gh}K,I$; the two successive derived bijections are computed by the ordinary ones on $p_hp_gK,I$. Exactness identifies $P_t(QK)$ with $Q(p_tK)$, as in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Precomposition by $Q(a^0_K)$ and postcomposition by $Q(b_I^{-1})$ therefore correspond by Step 1. The former is $a_{QK}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], and the latter is $c_M^{-1}$ by Step 2. Every derived object has a complex representative and every target has such an $I$; the Hom identifications are natural, including on localized morphisms. By the formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], naturality of the units and the triangle identities, a transformation $\tau:L_2\to L_1$ and $\sigma:R_1\to R_2$ satisfy $\sigma=\tau^c$ exactly when precomposition by $\tau$ on $\operatorname{Hom}(L_1X,Y)$ corresponds under the two adjunction bijections to postcomposition by $\sigma$ on $\operatorname{Hom}(X,R_1Y)$; this Yoneda check is elementary. This proves that $a$ and this particular $c^{-1}$ are conjugate under the specified derived adjunctions.

Put $L'=P_hP_g$, $R'=R_gR_h$ and $e'_M=\varepsilon_{h,M}\circ P_h(\varepsilon_{g,R_hM})$, the composite counit of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. By the definition of conjugation [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], $c_M^{-1}$ is the adjunct under $P_{gh}\dashv R_{gh}$ of $e'_M\circ a_{R'M}$. The adjunct-counit identity [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity] gives $\varepsilon_{gh,M}\circ P_{gh}(c_M^{-1})=e'_M\circ a_{R'M}$. Precompose with $P_{gh}(c_M)$ and cancel the inverse pair. This is exactly the counit equality in the item, with source $P_{gh}R_{gh}M$.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-projection-tensor-composition] to the ringed topoi $U_{\mathrm{proet}}\to V_{\mathrm{proet}}\to W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, with constant ring sheaf $A$ and their small site models. The operations and canonical adjunctions are exactly [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Its projection maps are the adjuncts of $(\varepsilon\otimes1)\mu$, which are exactly $\pi_t$ by the finite projection clause of [def-exchange-projection]. Its canonical tensor comparisons are the finite comparisons of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], including their compatibility with pullback composition. Steps 2–4 identify the direct-image comparison with the specified $c$ and normalize its counit. To write the cited composition equality with explicit endpoints, its source identification is $c_M\otimes1_N$ and its target identification is $R_gR_h(1_M\otimes a_N)\circ c_{M\otimes^LP_{gh}N}$. Substituting these two identifications into that equality gives precisely
$$R_gR_h(d_{M,N})\,c_{M\otimes^LP_{gh}N}\,\pi_{gh;M,N}=R_g(\pi_{h;M,P_gN})\,\pi_{g;R_hM,N}\,(c_M\otimes1_N).$$
All the hypotheses of the cited coherence lemma are ringed-topos hypotheses, with arbitrary derived arguments; none requires a projection isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map; categories.tex Tag 0DV0; existing ringed projection composition coherence

proof.text: The components in the counit equality are natural transformations, so that equality is natural in $M$. Projection naturality in both variables is part of [lem-sfb-ringed-projection-tensor-composition]. If either map is an identity, [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] makes $c$ the identity after the canonical unit identifications; its conjugate is the corresponding identity pullback comparison by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. The composite adjunction then has the remaining adjunction's counit, and the same ringed projection lemma says the identity projection is the identity. Substitution gives both asserted identity cases. Every preceding step used ordinary unbounded module categories and arbitrary $M,N$; no inverse of a projection map was taken.
